newsitem.title: USA: Lincoln Nat'l near Amer. States deal-sources.
newsitem.headline: Lincoln Nat'l near Amer. States deal-sources.

text.p: Lincoln National Corp is close to finding a buyer for its American States Financial Corp unit and may announce a deal for more than $2 billion as early as next week, sources familiar with the situation said.

Top contenders for the commercial property-casualty business were believed to include Hartford Financial Services Group Inc, Travelers Property Casualty Corp, Germany's Allianz AG Holding, SAFECO Corp and the U.K.'s General Accident Plc, sources said.
However, some sources said they believed Travelers has dropped out of the bidding.
Lincoln National, which has an 83 percent stake in American States, declined comment.
Hartford, Travelers and General Accident declined comment. SAFECO was not immediately available, but has previously declined comment.
Allianz was not immediately available for comment.
Zurich Insurance Co also has been reported to be interested in American States.
But reports that Zurich is in talks to buy mutual fund firm Scudder Stevens & Clark may make Zurich a less likely buyer of American States, an analyst said.
Sources said CNA Financial Corp also had expressed interest, but believe the company has since dropped out of the running. CNA declined comment.
"I think that what we've heard is that a decision will be made next week," one source familiar with the situation said.

The deal has attracted more interest than first expected as insurers, struggling for growth and faced with few attractive acquisition targets, remain unshaken by the property's rich valuation, analysts said.
"There are a couple of companies out there that need acquisitions for critical mass or to make them more important players geographically," Dillon Read analyst Michael Lewis said.
"It is a little expensive," Lewis said. "But there are no bargains in this sector right now."
Shares of American States were down 1/4 to 37-1/2 in morning trading, giving it a market value of about $2.250 billion.
Some analysts and bankers said they believe Lincoln National will get at least the market value of the company and could get as much as $40 a share or more.
"There are a lot more buyers than sellers out there," one analyst said.
And buyers are now willing to pay a bit more than was originally expected, Dillon Read's Lewis said.

Even so, the shares are up some 15 percent since late March when Lincoln National announced it was considering a sale of the business and the shares had run up ahead of that announcement on speculation that a deal might be in the works.
One banker said the European companies may have an edge in the bidding because they are generally less constrained by pressures to show immediate returns to shareholders.
"I think, realistically, it will be a European bidder," he said. "I don't think there are too many U.S. companies that could afford to do this," he said.
The ones that can, he said, may not be willing to make the winning bid "because it's a full price," he said.
In addition a U.S. company would need to consolidate it into its own operations to make the deal work, he said.

He said he did not believe a U.S. company would be able to achieve the cost savings needed to make such a deal work. On the other hand, he added, a U.S. company might achieve at least some cost savings, while a European company would probably find few if any savings, making the deal more costly.

Of the U.S. companies still believed to be in the running, Hartford, flush with cash from the spinoff of its life insurance unit and hungry for commercial property growth, could be one of the leading candidates, sources said.
SAFECO, they said, may not have sufficient financial resources to do this deal and Travelers may not be willing to pay such a steep price.
"It's attractive because there's nothing really wrong with ASX," an analyst said.
"It's a Main Street commercial book of business, well diversified, and fits well with national carriers," he said.
